summary_on_commit.description: "1": every head move of the main line gets a new summary; "0": only the birth of a file does (a failed birth summary is retried on the next head move either way). Embeddings follow `embed` alone.

embed.description: "1": every head move embeds the file section by section; "0": nothing is embedded, and `search` semantic and `ask` answer `not_indexed`.

ask_sections.description: How many sections, best first, `ask` hands the summarizer (plus at most one exact hit of the question's words).

section_lines.description: Window of a section in lines where no heading or page cuts the text (10 lines overlap); at most 400 sections a file, above that the windows grow.

nodes_max.description: The most nodes one head keeps in `nodes` (GH #944); more items keep the first ones in source order and mark the run `truncated`.

links_max.description: The most outgoing links one head keeps in `links`; more keep the first ones and mark the run `truncated`.

extract_max_bytes.description: The largest file (or PDF page text) the extractors parse; above it the run is marked `too_large` and has no nodes. The cap that keeps the extraction inside the cell's timeout.

key_depth.description: How deep `key:` nodes of JSON and TOML objects go.

agg_retries.description: How often the sync job (GH #947) tries again the directory rows whose compare-and-swap another writer won; above it the rows drift until the next change of a file under them.

dir_summary_children.description: The most entries (sub-directories and files, by path) `dir_summary` hands the summarizer, each as its one line.

description.purpose: What a file knows about itself, from its birth on (GH #903): after every head move of the main line it cuts the text view of the new version into sections, embeds them through `./embed`, has `./summarizer` write a one-line and a short summary and the file's topic tags, and writes `summaries`, `embeddings` and `files.oneline`. Before any model is asked, the head's nodes and links (a pure extractor chain, GH #944) replace the version's rows and every older one's in `nodes`, `links` and `node_runs`, and one `source_changed` leaves the hive; `node_runs.fvec` gets the file vector once the sections are embedded, and once the summary is stored for a head that is still living, one `source_described` (its one line and tags) leaves the hive. Every derive job ends with a sync job (GH #947) that moves the file's contribution -- bytes, nodes, file vector, tags -- into the `dirs` rows of all its ancestors as the difference to `contrib`; `in_dirs` starts one for a file that was removed or moved. It answers `search` with mode `semantic`, `ask` -- out of the embeddings of the one file and version asked about -- and `dir_summary`, the lazy one line of a directory; these are the operations of the hive that ask a model.
description.use_when: Inside `file-space` only: behind `./write` (and `./ws` on a commit) on `in_derive` and `in_dirs`, and behind the hive's `in_read` for `ask`, semantic `search` and `dir_summary`.
description.not_in_scope: No write of a file, no working version (they get nothing), no entities (Bau C), no model or endpoint of its own: `./embed` and `./summarizer` are the only doors out, and only this cell opens them.
description.emits_meaning: derive_store: store operations, every one with `file` in its `where` (`dirs` has no file), answered back on `cur_origin` `derive`. embed: texts to embed (the sections, or the question). summarize: the summary brief, the `ask` brief with the chosen lines, or the `dir_summary` brief with the directory's entries. answer: exactly one answer per `in_read` request, `op`, `op_id`, `caller` mirrored; `dir_summary` answers `{path, summary, fresh}` -- `fresh` true when this request made the summary, false when it is the stored one of an unchanged directory -- or `not_found` / `summary_failed`. derived: `{file, version, ok, oneline}` after an `in_derive` that carried `notify` "1" (also on failure), `caller` mirrored. source_changed: `{source, version (12 hex), path, fmt, parser, mark, nodes, links, tomb: false}` once per derive job whose version is still the living head after its node rows are written (before the summary and the embedding, whatever they do), no `caller` in the head; a version that is no longer head sends none. source_described: `{source, version (12 hex), path, oneline, tags}` -- one per stored summary of a living head, after `files.oneline` and the tags are written (the path the file has then), no `caller` in the head; none without a stored summary (a failed one, or none asked for under `summary_on_commit` "0") and none for a version that is no longer head. A catalog of the space's files reads it. A sync job sends nothing out of the cell.
description.consumes_meaning: in_derive `{file, version}` (hop `notify`, `caller`); in_dirs `{file}` (a file left or changed its directories: a remove, a move, a removal by a commit -- synced silently); in_read `{op, file, args}` for `ask` and semantic `search`, `{op: "dir_summary", args: {path}}` for a directory; `embedded` from `./embed`, `in_summary` from `./summarizer`, and the store's answers to its phases. A failed embedding or summary writes nothing of its own and leaves the rows there are (the nodes of the head are already written, and the file still counts in its directories, without tags or vector); the next head move tries again.
